name: Sir Keir Starmer
role: Prime Minister & First Lord of the Treasury
bio: Former Director of Public Prosecutions and QC. Elected Labour leader in 2020 and became Prime Minister in July 2024 with a mission-driven government framework.
keyStance: Strict fiscal rules, 5 national missions, closer security ties with EU, NHS 10-year turnaround.

name: Rachel Reeves
bio: First female Chancellor in British history. Former Bank of England economist who champions 'securonomics'—active industrial strategy combined with strict fiscal debt rules.
keyStance: Balancing day-to-day spending with revenues, reforming fiscal borrowing rules to boost capital investment, no rise in basic/higher income tax or VAT.

name: Yvette Cooper
bio: Veteran parliamentarian and former Home Affairs Select Committee Chair, overseeing borders, police standards, counter-terrorism, and public safety.
keyStance: New Border Security Command, cross-border European policing pacts to dismantle smuggler gangs, neighbourhood policing guarantee.

name: David Lammy
role: Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
bio: Harvard Law graduate and prominent internationalist, driving Labour's 'progressive realism' foreign policy doctrine.
keyStance: Reconnecting with Europe, unshakeable support for NATO and Ukraine, balanced Middle East diplomacy with two-state solution commitment.

name: John Healey
bio: Long-serving defence specialist who led Labour's shadow defence brief before entering government, spearheading the Strategic Defence Review.
keyStance: Roadmap to 2.5% of GDP defence spending, UK-Germany defence treaty, modernized procurement, prioritising British-made military equipment.

name: Wes Streeting
role: Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
bio: Dynamic health reformer advocating for 'reform alongside investment' in the NHS, shifting focus from acute hospital care to prevention and community care.
keyStance: Cut waiting lists by 40,000 appointments a week, utilize spare private hospital capacity, digitalise patient records, 10-year NHS workforce plan.

name: Kemi Badenoch
bio: Elected Conservative Party leader in late 2024. Former Business and Trade Secretary and Equalities Minister, known for institutional critiques and pro-market principles.
keyStance: Dismantling bureaucratic state interference, free enterprise revival, rigorous cultural clarity, reducing welfare dependency.

name: Mel Stride
bio: Former Treasury Select Committee Chair and Work and Pensions Secretary, known for technical economic scrutiny and fiscal discipline.
keyStance: Opposing tax rises on enterprise and pensions, shrinking the administrative state, reversing employer National Insurance hikes.

name: Chris Philp
bio: Former Policing and Crime Minister, focusing on anti-social behaviour crackdowns, visible policing, and immigration enforcement.
keyStance: Re-establishing strong immigration deterrence, strict deportation timelines, tough sentencing for knife crime.

name: Dame Priti Patel
bio: Former Home Secretary and International Development Secretary, championing bilateral global trade and robust international security alliances.
keyStance: Strong deterrent posture against hostile states, robust Atlantic alliance, resisting European institutional entanglement.

name: James Cartlidge
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Defence
bio: Former Defence Procurement Minister with deep insight into military supply chains and equipment delivery programs.
keyStance: Immediate commitment to 2.5% of GDP defence spending by 2030, continuous-at-sea nuclear deterrent funding, boosting munitions reserves.

name: Nigel Farage
bio: Long-time political figure, Brexit architect, and broadcaster. Returned as Reform UK leader in June 2024 and won election to Parliament.
keyStance: Freeze non-essential immigration, leave ECHR, raise income tax threshold to £20,000, scrap Net Zero, complete NHS patient voucher choice.

name: Richard Tice
bio: Businessman and property entrepreneur, serving as Reform UK's deputy leader and treasury/economic spokesperson.
keyStance: Cut corporation tax to 15%, lift employer NI threshold, unleash British oil and gas extraction, abolish IR35.

name: Lee Anderson
role: Chief Whip & Spokesperson for Home Affairs
bio: Former coal miner and former Conservative Deputy Chairman, widely followed for blunt populist commentary and working-class representation.
keyStance: Zero tolerance on illegal boat crossings, immediate detention and removal, stop taxpayer funding of hotel accommodations for migrants.

name: Rupert Lowe
bio: Former Southampton FC Chairman and businessman, campaigning against excessive civil service bureaucracy and agricultural Net Zero burdens.
keyStance: Slash Whitehall staffing by 50%, protect British farming, scrap green subsidies inflating household bills.

name: Sir Ed Davey
bio: Former Energy and Climate Change Secretary who led the Liberal Democrats to their highest seat total in over a century (72 MPs) in 2024.
keyStance: Universal access to GP appointments within 7 days, £5bn social care package, ban water company executive bonuses, rejoin EU Single Market.

name: Daisy Cooper
bio: Deputy Leader and former Health Spokesperson, leading the Lib Dem economic push on fair taxation and public service reinvestment.
keyStance: Tax tech giants and windfall oil profits, reverse real-terms cuts to school budgets, support small high-street businesses.

name: Helen Morgan
role: Spokesperson for Health and Social Care
bio: Chartered accountant who won the historic North Shropshire by-election; champion for rural healthcare and ambulance response times.
keyStance: Dedicated fund for ambulance waiting times, mental health parity in all NHS trusts, free personal care modeled on Scotland.

name: Calum Miller
role: Spokesperson for Defence and Foreign Affairs
bio: Former senior civil servant with extensive foreign policy and defence background.
keyStance: Ensure UK meets 2.5% GDP defence spending responsibly, strengthen NATO European pillar, uphold international humanitarian law.

name: Carla Denyer
bio: Renewable energy engineer who defeated Labour's Shadow Culture Secretary to enter Parliament; leading green voice on housing, climate, and public health.
keyStance: 1% to 2% wealth tax on assets over £10m, rent controls, quadruple green energy generation, reverse NHS privatization.

name: Adrian Ramsay
bio: Experienced environmental strategist and former deputy leader, elected MP for rural Waveney Valley.
keyStance: Fair farm subsidies protecting biodiversity, nationalise water and railways, halt all new oil/gas exploration.

name: John Swinney
role: Party Leader & First Minister of Scotland
bio: Veteran Scottish statesman who served as Deputy First Minister for nearly a decade before returning as leader to stabilize the party in 2024.
keyStance: Scottish self-determination, scrap the two-child benefit cap across the UK, protect Scottish NHS funding, rejoin the EU.

name: Stephen Flynn
bio: Sharp orator and energy advocate representing North East Scotland, leading the party's Westminster parliamentary strategy.
keyStance: Just transition for North Sea energy workers without reckless cliff-edges, demand full devolution of employment and migration law.

name: Rhun ap Iorwerth
role: Party Leader & Member of the Senedd
bio: Former BBC broadcaster who took over Plaid Cymru leadership in 2023, unifying the party around progressive Welsh decentralization and community renewal.
keyStance: Replacement of the Barnett formula with needs-based funding, HS2 consequential funding for Welsh railways, Welsh independence referendum roadmap.

name: Liz Saville Roberts
bio: Privy Councillor and Westminster leader since 2017, vocal advocate for judicial devolution and equal treatment of Wales.
keyStance: Devolution of policing and justice to Wales, renewable energy wealth retention for local communities, rural medical access.

name: Movement Council Spokesperson
bio: Civic assembly representing traditionalist British restoration, civil liberties, and free market constitutionalism.
keyStance: Abolish Net Zero statutes, repeal domestic legislation eroding free speech, constitutional referendums, national industrial revival.
